ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, this is a pedigree chart of a certain single-gene autosomal recessive hereditary disease (the dark-colored individuals are patients with this hereditary disease, and the rest are phenotypically normal individuals). The incidence of this hereditary disease is higher in consanguineous marriage. Assuming that the probability that the two individuals in generation Ⅳ in the figure marry and give birth to a child with this hereditary disease is 1/48, then should Ⅱ-1, Ⅲ-1, and Ⅲ-4 be homozygotes or heterozygotes to obtain this probability?

Ⅱ-1 and Ⅱ-2 marry, and their offspring is Ⅲ-2; Ⅲ-1 and Ⅲ-2 marry, and their offspring is the generation Ⅳ individual Ⅳ-1. Ⅱ-3 and Ⅱ-4 marry, and their offspring is Ⅲ-3; Ⅲ-3 and Ⅲ-4 marry, and their offspring is the generation Ⅳ individual Ⅳ-2. The question asks, when the probability that the two individuals in generation Ⅳ marry and have an affected child is 1/48, whether Ⅱ-1, Ⅲ-1, and Ⅲ-4 should be homozygotes or heterozygotes. Then reason: This disease is an autosomal recessive hereditary disease, and the genotype of affected individuals is aa. Ⅰ-1 and Ⅰ-3 are affected, so both are aa. Ⅱ-2 and Ⅱ-3 are normal children of Ⅰ-1, so they must receive a from the affected father, and because they are phenotypically normal, their genotypes are both Aa; Ⅱ-4 is a normal child of Ⅰ-3, so also must be Aa. If Ⅱ-1, Ⅲ-1, and Ⅲ-4 are all normal homozygotes AA: in the left branch, Ⅱ-1 AA × Ⅱ-2 Aa, then the probability that Ⅲ-2 is a carrier Aa is 1/2; Ⅲ-1 is AA, so the probability that Ⅳ-1 is a carrier is (1/2)×(1/2)=1/4. In the right branch, Ⅱ-3 Aa × Ⅱ-4 Aa, and Ⅲ-3 is phenotypically normal, so the conditional probability that Ⅲ-3 is a carrier Aa is 2/3; Ⅲ-4 is AA, so the probability that Ⅳ-2 is a carrier is (2/3)×(1/2)=1/3. If the two individuals in generation Ⅳ are both carriers, the probability of giving birth to an affected child aa is 1/4, so the total probability is (1/4)×(1/3)×(1/4)=1/48. This result exactly matches the probability given in the question stem. Therefore, Ⅱ-1, Ⅲ-1, and Ⅲ-4 should be normal homozygotes AA.
